results.title: Clark-Cameron system (Levy area)
results.challenge: The counterexample of the strong-convergence literature: no scheme built from the Brownian increments alone beats strong order 1/2 on U = int S dW1 (Clark & Cameron 1980). Fine sub-increments are supplied so a Milstein scheme that assembles the Levy area from them converges at order 1; Euler-Maruyama at the graded step does not.

1-levy-area-milstein-drift-corrected.one_sentence: Milstein with Levy area I_(2,1) assembled from dW_sub and mu*I_(0,1) replaced by its conditional mean 0.5*mu*dt*dW1; strong order 1.0.

2-levy-area-milstein.one_sentence: Standard Milstein with Levy area I_(2,1) from dW_sub, omitting the mu*I_(0,1) term; strong order 1.0.

3-step-increment-conditional-expectation.one_sentence: Control scheme using only step increments dW, iterated integrals replaced by conditional expectations (trapezoid on U); strong order 0.5, expected to miss the 2% gate.

results.title: Kubo oscillator (Stratonovich)
results.challenge: The textbook Stratonovich system (Kloeden & Platen; Milstein, Repin & Tretyakov 2002): the exact flow is a rotation and conserves |X|. Reading the coefficients as Ito solves a different equation whose amplitude grows by e^{sigma^2 T/2}.

1-cayley-midpoint.one_sentence: Stratonovich implicit midpoint (Cayley rational rotation), norm-preserving per path, strong order 1, dt=0.04.

2-stochastic-heun.one_sentence: Was explicit Stratonovich Heun; bias retry replaced it with a 4-stage RK step on f*dt+g*dW (one shared dW), dt=0.04.

3-milstein.one_sentence: Was Ito Milstein; bias retry rewrote it into the Cayley midpoint step (identical to plan 1), dt=0.04.

results.title: Ait-Sahalia interest-rate model
results.challenge: Ait-Sahalia's (1996) strongly nonlinear short rate: a 1/X drift that repels the origin, a superlinear X^2 mean reversion and an X^{3/2} diffusion. Backward Euler-Maruyama preserves positivity (Szpruch, Mao, Higham & Pan 2011); the explicit step overshoots into X < 0 and the variance it reports is garbage.

1-lamperti-trapezoidal.one_sentence: Lamperti transform Z = X^(-1/2) (additive noise) with a drift-implicit trapezoidal step, dt=0.02, 200k paths; family implicit.

2-drift-implicit-milstein.one_sentence: Drift-implicit Milstein directly in X with a per-step cubic solve (unique positive root), dt=0.02, 200k paths; family milstein.

3-drift-implicit-euler.one_sentence: Drift-implicit Euler baseline in X with the same cubic solve, no Milstein term, dt=0.02, 200k paths; family implicit.

results.title: Wright-Fisher diffusion with mutation
results.challenge: Kimura's diffusion of population genetics (the Jacobi diffusion in finance), bounded in [0,1] with both boundaries attainable at these mutation rates. A boundary-preserving step is required; clipping to [0,1] stays finite and biases the mean by 8%.

1-beta-moment-matched.one_sentence: Per-step Beta draw matching the exact one-step conditional mean and variance, dt=0.04 (25 steps), support-preserving.

2-milstein-reflected.one_sentence: Scalar Milstein with bounded correction 0.25σ²(1−2X)(dW²−dt), reflected into [0,1] each step.

3-euler-maruyama-projected.one_sentence: Euler–Maruyama with per-step projection onto [0,1]; control plan, expected to miss the 5% mean gate.

results.title: Merton jump diffusion (European call)
results.challenge: Merton's (1976) lognormal jump diffusion, the first jump-diffusion option model, at a published parameter set. The only non-Gaussian driver in the benchmark; the compensator is the decision -- dropping it moves the mean by 1.4% (inside the gate) and the price by 19%.

1-milstein-cv.one_sentence: Scalar Milstein on the diffusion with multiplicative jumps at step ends; call price with X_T control variate whose scheme mean is known exactly.

2-weak-order2-taylor.one_sentence: Kloeden-Platen simplified order-2.0 weak Taylor scheme with same jump handling; plain MC price.

3-euler-maruyama.one_sentence: Plain Euler-Maruyama with same jump handling; plain MC price (discretised baseline).

results.title: Stochastic SIS epidemic
results.challenge: The SDE SIS model of Gray, Greenhalgh, Hu, Mao & Pan (2011) at its own Example 5.2: a superlinear sigma I (N - I) diffusion on (0, N) and a stiff logistic drift. Explicit Euler diverges at the graded step; the same splitting with the noise step clipped in I rather than taken in the logit chart biases the mean by 10%.

1-logit-strang-heun.one_sentence: Logit-coordinate Strang splitting, exact logistic half-flows, Heun on bounded drift plus additive noise.

2-strang-milstein-in-i.one_sentence: Strang splitting with exact logistic half-flows and Milstein noise step in I.

3-logit-drift-implicit-euler.one_sentence: Backward-Euler on full logit-coordinate drift, Newton with bisection fallback.

results.title: Underdamped Langevin dynamics (BAOAB)
results.challenge: The workhorse of molecular sampling, at moderate friction. Leimkuhler & Matthews (2012/13) compare integrators by the invariant measure they sample: BAOAB's bias on Var(q) is a hundredth of the gate here, Euler-Maruyama's is 2.8x the gate while linearly stable.

results.title: Geometric-average Asian option (Kemna-Vorst)
results.challenge: Kemna & Vorst's (1990) closed-form Asian option, the standard MLMC test problem (Giles 2008). The only entry grading a time integral along the path: an endpoint Riemann sum of int ln S dt misprices the call by 3.4% against a 1% gate; the trapezoid by 0.02%.

1-milstein-bridge-cv.one_sentence: Milstein steps on S, trapezoid+bridge-corrected integral of ln S, control variate on discounted S(T).

2-log-euler-bridge.one_sentence: Log-Euler (exact per-step law) with bridge-corrected trapezoid integral, plain MC.

3-euler-maruyama-trapezoid.one_sentence: Plain Euler-Maruyama with trapezoid rule on grid nodes, discretised baseline.
